expectations.text: A spec for the overdue feature exists under OUTPUT_DIR/repo/docs/product-specs/, either as a new file with a new prefix or as new criteria appended to tickets.md or cli.md with fresh IDs; the transcript or spec says which was chosen and why.
expectations.evidence: Amended tickets.md (new '## Overdue tickets' section, TKT-014..TKT-016) and cli.md (CLI-010, CLI-011; CLI-001, CLI-006 amended). Reason, from the final message: 'I amended the existing specs rather than creating a new file, because the repo organizes specs by feature area and overdue builds on TKT-005 and the `list` command.'

expectations.text: The spec has a one-paragraph intro, a `Prefix:` line, and a Non-goals section with at least two non-goals that are real boundaries (for example no notifications, no SLA pause on weekends, no change to the event log format).
expectations.evidence: Intro paragraph: 'Overdue marking shows support agents which unfinished tickets have passed their due time. Agents see the overdue tickets in the full list...'. File keeps 'Prefix: `TKT`.'. 'Not in scope:' lists 7 boundaries (no fourth state, no lateness amount, no alerts, no TKT-005/business-hours change, no filters, no due-soon warning, no change to full-list order). Also 'Goals:'.

expectations.text: At least five criteria headed `### PREFIX-NNN: Title` with zero-padded three-digit numbers (a letter suffix such as TKT-014A is allowed), unique within the file; no `**Testable:**` lines. Body length is judged separately: most bodies are one to three sentences, and a longer body is noted, not a failure.
expectations.evidence: 5 new criteria from the diff: TKT-014, TKT-015, TKT-016, CLI-010, CLI-011 (exactly the minimum). Correct headings, unique, no Testable lines. CLI-011 has two paragraphs (8 sentences) and is longer than typical; the others have 2-3 sentences.

expectations.text: Criteria cover: the OVERDUE marker in `list` output; the `overdue` command's filter; the oldest-due-first order; a ticket exactly at its due time; closed tickets (either excluded, or an open question); and what the user sees when nothing is overdue (output and exit code).
expectations.evidence: Marker: CLI-010 '#<id> [<priority>] <state> OVERDUE <title>' + example. Filter: TKT-016 'returns only the tickets that are overdue'; CLI-011 'Closed tickets do not appear'. Order: TKT-016 'due time ascending... ID ascending'. Exact due: TKT-014 'A ticket whose due time equals the current time is not overdue yet.' Closed: TKT-015 'never overdue'. Empty: CLI-011 'With no overdue tickets it prints nothing and exits with code 0.' Stated as a criterion; also listed as an assumption in questions.md Q6.

expectations.text: Every criterion body is behavioral: no function, class, module, or file names (such as TicketService, due_at, cli.py); outcomes are described as what the user sees in the CLI output or exit code.
expectations.evidence: No implementation names in new bodies (impl_words=0).

expectations.text: The spec respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue is a derived state computed from the ticket's due time and is not written to the event log; if the spec proposes a new event kind, it flags that as a change to LOG-002 and the invariants needing sign-off.
expectations.evidence: 'Overdue is a view, not a record... No event records that a ticket became overdue, and the log does not change when one does, see INV-002. Replay still yields the same due times, see LOG-009.' Non-goal: 'A fourth ticket state.' CLI-011: 'appends no event to the log'. INV-001 not cited in the spec (the final message cites it).

expectations.text: The spec does not contradict TKT-005 (due time by priority) or TKT-013 (listing order of `list`): it reuses the existing due time and states how OVERDUE interacts with the existing list order rather than redefining it.
expectations.evidence: Intro: 'The due time comes from TKT-005.' Non-goal stated outright: 'A change to the order of the full list. TKT-013 is unchanged.' CLI-006 keeps 'in ID order, see TKT-013'; CLI-010: 'The line of a ticket that is not overdue does not change.'

expectations.text: Open questions are listed at the end of the spec (or in OUTPUT_DIR/questions.md) and assumptions are marked inline; none of them is silently resolved in a criterion.

The blocking assumptions (marker beside the state, closed never overdue, overdue line = list line) are only in questions.md: no inline TODOs and not in the in-file list. Not silent, because questions.md covers them with criterion IDs.
